Can you explain the main options in simple terms?
• Just now
Seen • Just now
Absolutely! Here's a simple breakdown of the main spirit categories we offer:
Whiskey — the broadest category, includes:
Bourbon: American whiskey made primarily from corn. Smooth, sweet, with notes of vanilla and caramel. Great for beginners.
Scotch: Whisky from Scotland. Can range from light and floral to rich and smoky. More complex flavors.
Rye: Spicier, bolder whiskey with a peppery kick. Made from rye grain.
Tequila: Made from agave in Mexico. Ranges from fresh and citrusy (Blanco) to smooth and oak-aged (Añejo). Perfect for sipping or cocktails.
Rum: Made from sugarcane or molasses. Can be light and mixable or dark and rich with caramel notes.
Vodka: Clean, neutral spirit. Very versatile for cocktails or enjoyed chilled.
Gin: Botanical spirit flavored with juniper and herbs. Ranges from classic London Dry to modern floral styles.
Starting tips:
Bourbon and Tequila are often the most approachable for beginners
Start with lower-proof options (around 40% ABV)
Try tasting sets to explore different styles before committing to full bottles

How do I use it properly the very first time?
• Just now
Seen • Just now
Great question! Here's your step-by-step guide for tasting bourbon properly the first time:
Step 1: Pour & Observe
Pour about 1-2 ounces into a glass (any short glass works, but a tulip-shaped glass is ideal). Look at the color — notice the amber tones.
Step 2: Smell First
Bring the glass to your nose and take a gentle sniff. Don't stick your nose right in — the alcohol can overwhelm you. Notice the aromas: vanilla, caramel, oak, spices?
Step 3: The First Sip
Take a small sip and roll it over your tongue and around your mouth. Don't swallow immediately — let it coat your palate. This prepares your mouth for the flavor.
Step 4: Savor & Identify
Notice the flavors: Sweet? Spicy? Woody? Fruity? Pay attention to the texture and intensity too.
Three ways to drink it:
Neat (no ice, no water) — Best way to taste the true character
On the rocks (with ice) — Use large ice cubes so it chills without watering down too much
With a splash of water — Actually releases more flavors and lowers the alcohol burn
My advice for your first time: Start neat, take one small sip. If it's too strong, add one ice cube or a tiny splash of water. Be patient with it — sip slowly, don't gulp!
